# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-18 (Extended v140)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (March-April Year 5, transitioning to late April Year 5)**: Paris—Rue Plumet (Valjean's primary house); Rue de Babylone (secret passage exit); Luxembourg; Salpêtrière district; garden near Austerlitz settlement; harbor town of Dunstead (English provinces); Wilwick (hill farms); various secondary locations. **March-April environment**: Days growing longer, winter departing, April as daybreak of summer, fresh charming gleams, nature influencing human heart. Subsequently: evening decline, propitious hours, no cat in lane, smoke lying flat over fields, wind from water smelling of salt and tar, baker's boy late, line at oven long.

## Primary Locations
**RUE PLUMET HOUSE**: Single-story pavilion in deserted Rue Plumet with garden approximately one-and-a-half acres. Two ground-floor rooms, two first-floor chambers, downstairs kitchen, upstairs boudoir, attic. Behind pavilion: narrow courtyard, low building (two rooms, cellar). Secret-spring door masked in building communicates via long narrow paved winding corridor to Rue de Babylone quarter-league distant. Originally built mid-last-century as mistress-house; October 1829: Valjean hired and repaired as M. Fauchelevent. **Garden characteristics**: Left uncultivated; breathes melancholy, solitude, liberty, absence of man, presence of God; ancient padlocked gate twisted, tottering; nature filled with shade arranged for love.

## Jean Valjean's Recovery and Renewed Contentment (October 1831—March-April Year 5)
**The wound and illness**: Day following Jondrette visit, Valjean appeared with large inflamed wound on left arm resembling burn (origin unclear). Detained in house one month with fever; refused doctor. Cosette deserted pavilion, devoted herself entirely to his care, read travel books. **Valjean undergoing new birth**: his happiness reviving in ineffable rays; Luxembourg, young stranger Marius, Cosette's coldness—all clouds upon his soul growing dim. Thought to himself: "I imagined all that. I am an old fool."

**March-April transformation**: Cosette perceived father suffering less, convalescing, appearing happy. Experienced contentment so gentle and natural she did not perceive it. April arrived—daybreak of summer, fresh and gay, causing nature's charming gleams to pass from sky, trees, meadows, flowers into human heart.

**Charitable activities resumed**: One former happiness remained: carry bread to hungry, clothing to cold. Cosette often accompanied Valjean on visits to poor; recovered remnants of former free intercourse; when day had been good assisting many in distress, Cosette rather merry in evening.

**Thénardier acceptance**: His happiness so great that horrible discovery of Thénardiers in Jondrette hovel, though unexpected, glided over unnoticed. He succeeded in escape; all trace lost—he cared not. Only thought to pity them. "Here they are in prison, incapacitated for harm," he reasoned. "But what lamentable family in distress!"

## Cosette's Recovery and New Distraction (March-April Year 5)
**Blackness departing**: Too young to escape penetrating influence of April joy resembling herself. Insensibly, without suspecting, blackness departed from her spirit. In spring, sad souls grow light as light falls into cellars at midday. No longer sad, though did not account for it to herself.

**Morning contentment**: About ten o'clock after breakfast, enticed father into garden for quarter-hour. Paced sunlight before steps, supporting his left arm. Did not perceive she laughed every moment and was happy.

**Grief's convalescence**: Cosette's poignant lively grief of four-five months previously entered convalescence without her consciousness. Nature, spring, youth, love for father, gayety of birds and flowers caused something resembling forgetfulness to filter gradually, drop by drop, into virgin young soul. Fire not wholly extinct; layers of ashes formed. Hardly felt painful burning spot any longer.

**New officer distraction (late April Year 5)**: Same week, noticed very handsome officer of lancers—wasp-like waist, delicious uniform, young girl's cheeks, sword under arm, waxed moustaches, glazed schapka. Light hair, prominent blue eyes, round face, vain, insolent, good-looking; quite reverse of Marius. Cigar in mouth. Cosette thought officer likely belonged to regiment in barracks on Rue de Babylone. **Claim**: This observation occurred precisely when Marius descending heavily toward agony, saying "If I could but see her before I die!"—Had wish realized, beholding Cosette gazing at lancer, would not utter word and expire with grief.

## Marius Pontmercy: Continued Psychological and Financial Crisis (March-April Year 5)
**Status unchanged**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years estranged from grandfather. **Financial crisis continuing**: Borrowing five francs from Courfeyrac. Poverty returned; icy breath felt. Cannot focus on work—turning celebrated German quarrel into French. Sees star between himself and paper.

**Psychological descent (April Year 5)**: **Claim—Marius now descending heavily towards agony, saying "If I could but see her before I die!"** Passion precipitated him into chimæras without object or bottom. Lost faculty of working toward fixed goal. Judgment disassociated from hope. Meditation turns to reproach. Reflects dolefully on idleness, paralysis of soul gaining, night growing more dense. Yet happy, even in anguish.

## Gavroche's Adventure and Montparnasse Encounter (Late April Year 5)
**Gavroche's hunger**: One evening, little Gavroche had nothing to eat; had not dined preceding day either; becoming tiresome. Resolved to secure supper. Strolled beyond Salpêtrière into deserted regions. Reached settlement appearing to be village of Austerlitz. **Previously noticed**: old garden haunted by old man and old woman, passable apple-tree, unsecured fruit-house. Garden abutted solitary unpaved lane bordered with brushwood, separated by hedge. One apple: supper; one apple: life.

**The assault witnessed**: Directed steps toward garden, found lane, recognized apple-tree, examined hedge. Day declining, no cat in lane, hour propitious. Began scaling hedge, suddenly paused—someone talking in garden. Peeped through break in hedge. At foot of hedge, recumbent stone forming bench: old man seated, old woman standing, grumbling. Old man was **Father Mabeuf**.

**Montparnasse present**: A second figure—straight, firm, slender, regulating pace by first; suppleness and agility discernible. Fierce disquieting aspect, called _an elegant_: good-shape hat, black well-cut coat of fine cloth, well-fitted waist, erect head with robust grace, pale profile of young man in dim light with rose in mouth. **This second form was Montparnasse** (eighteen years old, redoubtable ruffian). Gavroche deliberated: interfere? One weakness aiding another—laughing matter for Montparnasse. Old man and child would make two mouthfuls.

**The unexpected reversal**: Attack took place abruptly, hideously—tiger on wild ass, spider on fly. Montparnasse tossed rose, bounded upon old man, seized collar, grasped clung. Gavroche restrained scream. Moment later: one beneath other, groaning, struggling, knee of marble upon breast. **Unexpected outcome: Montparnasse lay on earth; old man on top.**

**Gavroche's theft**: Gavroche assured himself Father Mabeuf still sitting on bench, probably asleep. Gamin emerged from thicket, began crawling after motionless Montparnasse in dark. Came up without seen/heard, gently insinuated hand into back pocket of fine black cloth frock-coat, seized purse, withdrew hand, crawled away like adder through shadows. Montparnasse, no reason on guard, engaged in thought first time in life, perceived nothing. When Gavroche attained Father Mabeuf's point, flung purse over hedge, fled fast as legs carried.

## Supporting Characters and Secondary Locations
**Father Mabeuf**: Old man in garden; apparently capable of extraordinary physical prowess despite age; sitting on bench when Gavroche observes aftermath.

**Montparnasse**: Elegant ruffian, eighteen years old, rose in mouth, well-dressed in fine black coat; unexpectedly defeated in assault on Father Mabeuf; thief victim of child pickpocket Gavroche.

**English provincial figures** (mentioned, location/function unclear): Rovus Prydenridge, Nerine Prydenridge, Movie Prydenridge, Havie Prydenridge, Luena Stenenridge, Rozek Stenenridge, Isric Thornmere, Zavus Thornmere, Islan Thornmere, Wenelle, Yera, Lurald Stenworth, Elmhaven. **Note**: Status, affiliations, relevance to main narrative uncertain; appear as passing observations in Dunstead/English provinces context. Conversations concern weather, harvest, lame horse, river conditions, stories, aching back, commerce.

## Key Facts and States
- **Valjean's age**: Old enough to have passed Barrière du Maine thirty-five years prior (chain-gang procession memory).
- **Cosette's emotional state**: Grief convalescent; blackness departed; new distraction (lancer officer) occupying attention; love for Marius apparently dormant/forgotten.
- **Marius's state**: Descending toward agony; desperate longing to see Cosette before death; unaware of her attention to officer.
- **Gavroche's status**: Street child, homeless, hungry, clever pickpocket, observer of events, compassionate (restrained from interfering).
- **Thénardiers**: In prison, incapacitated for harm; Valjean indifferent to their fate.
- **Season**: Transitioned from October 1831 (chain-gang) through February (illness) to March-April Year 5 (recovery and new emotional currents).
